title.narrative: IDEA - stöd till Sudan´s transition till demokrati

description.narrative:
Objectives of the intervention
The overall purpose of the contribution is to support Sudans transition to a democratic system. It contributes to SDG 16 (to promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels) and SDG 5 (Ensure womens full and effective participation and equal opportunities for leadership at all levels of decision making in political, economic and public life.)
The objectives with the contribution are to contribute to the following:
• Improved citizens awareness on a transitional processes and democratic governance. • Policymakers within political parties and the government apply increased knowledge and skills to make more informed choices regarding democracy reforms • The National Election Commission apply increased knowledge and skills to recognize and respond to complexities and risks in the electoral processes and effectively implement the Electoral Cycle Approach • Civil society (with a focus on womens groups) and media in Sudan apply increased knowledge and skills to engage with constitution makers, policymakers in political parties and government and the National Election Commission democratically and effectively and promote broad public participation in the process.
After the military coup October, 2021 the interventions were revised and technical assistance was no longer provided to the government or its institutions. The programme focus on a) training and strengthening civil society on democratic issues with a focus on young people and women and b) cooperating with other organisations to resist the closure of civil society. Continued support to women political participation and an assessment of the framework for disabled persons' opportunities to participate in elections. After that the civil war started in 2023, all activities focusing on electoral issues have been cancelled as well. Instead, the IIDEA prioritises the strengthening of the expertise of various parties and organisations on the links between peace and democratic governance and to enhance women's political participation at all levels. IIDEA is implementing its programme remotely and is more inclusive of the Diaspora in exile.

Projektets övergripande mål är att stödja den demokratiska övergången i Sudan genom att upprätta mekanismer för dialog och konsensusuppbyggnad med fokus på delstatsnivå; stärka kapaciteten för NEC (National Election Committee) att leverera rättvisa och fredliga val; öka kvinnors deltagande och representation i politiska processer; samt stärka medborgarnas kunskap om politiska processer och demokratiska styrning. Det förväntas att Sudans övergångsperiod och processer som initierats av transitionsregeringen kan leda till demokrati, men är i behov av kapasitetsstärkande åtgärder. Projektet är ett komplement till EU´s insats för att stärka demokrati i Sudan och som genomförs av International IDEA. Det är emellertid två fristående program. Programmet sträcker sig över tre år (2020-2023) och budgeten är 45,3 MSEK

The overall objective is to support the democratic transition of Sudan by supporting the establishment of mechanisms for dialogue and consensus-building on the transition processes; strengthen the capacity of NEC (National Election Committee) deliver credible and peaceful elections; enhance women participation and representation in political processes, and strengthen citizens awareness on the transitional processes and the broader democratic governance practices. It is anticipated that Sudan’s transition period and processes will provide an opportunity for the country’s transition to democracy. The contribution is a complement to EU´s project for strengthening democracy in Sudan and is implemented by International IDEA. The project is complementary to the EU´s contribution to strengthening the democracy in Sudan and is implemented by IDEA. However, they are two independent projects. The duration of the project is 2020-2023, and the total budget is 45,3 MSEK.

title.narrative: Agreeement Sweden and International IDEA Sudan

description.narrative:
Examples of results achieved The results below are from the 2023 annual reporting. A new result report is due end of September 2024. Like the other national and international CSOs, International IDEAs office in Khartoum has been looted with all assets stolen. Due to the deteriorated security situation in Khartoum, most the staff have fled to some neighbouring countries but three staff are still in Sudan and in safe regions including Port Sudan. All I- IDEA staff are safe and working remotely including those that are still in Sudan. Apart from the knowledge production, implementation of program activities was suspended for three months. Later, I IDEA adjusted workplans with necessary changes on program delivery approaches and activity implementation. Some activities are being implemented in person in neighbouring countries such as workshops and dialogue events. Others are being implemented virtually.
Some of the results that has been achieved during the last reporting period June 2022-June 2023 are: International IDEA published a comparative study on the voting rights of IDPs in Sudan Advancing the voting rights of internally displaced communities in Sudan and the study Assessing Sudans electoral legal framework. The studies were published on International IDEAs Website in both English and Arabic. The link to the published studies were widely shared with the national partners, civil society, and other stakeholders concerned with the transitional process. International IDEA completed the first cohort of the Young Womens Democracy Academy (YWDA) successfully in 2022. The Swedish Ambassador in Khartoum visited the Academy and met the young women. Several of the women were after the training assigned to positions in which their newfound knowledge was put to good use. The second cohort was launched in March 2023 and was planned to continue until May 2023. Unfortunately, the eruption of war in Sudan in April 2023 stopped the program halfway through, but there are discussions to continue digitally. International IDEA conducted a situation analysis to address challenges and issues regarding PWDs' political participation and representation within the democratic transition processes. Also, to initiate a platform that includes all the relevant stakeholders to support the political participation and representation of PWDs. On 16 February the validation meeting was conducted for the final draft of The Situation Analysis on the political participation of persons with Disability.The final report is now in the publication process. ALAlag disseminate its radio shows during the reporting period. All produced materials considered diversity and covered different local communities issues regarding women political participation. The materials included drama addressing womens political participation, IDPs from a gender perspective, women in war zones, and freedom of expression and gender equality. It was sent at local radio stations in several states. The outputs included All produced materials considered diversity and covered different local communities issues regarding women political participation. The materials included drama addressing womens political participation, IDPs from a gender perspective, women in war zones, and freedom of expression and gender equality. The outputs included 8 drama plays, each 30 minutes long, 2 long radio drama plays, each 50 minutes long. 2 radio drama series in 10 10minutes episodes, 8 audio songs encouraging women political participation, 6 Public Statements and one operetta about womens participation in constitution building. Additionally, during the reporting period Al Alaq conducted three Youth capacity building forums on the democratic transition issues (Red Sea State Blue Nile and River Nile) International IDEA and its national partner SUDO conducted a dialogue facilitator workshop and 17 dialogue sessions for resistance committees, multi stakeholders dialogue platforms and workshops, which have reached a total of 470 people. The workshops were conducted in River Nile, Red Sea White Nile, South Kordofan, West Kordofan, River Nile , White Nile North Kordofan and South Darfur. Furthermore, a workshop in Gezira was conducted with on citizenship, accepting others and managing diversity. Additionally, IIDEA conducted a newly added activity Election Lab, which is a platform of national experts on election. The Lab is composed of 10 to 15 of Sudanese election experts Four labs were organised during the reporting period with support from Sida and EU. This activity was interrupted by the sudden conflict in Sudan and will resume virtually in the future, with support from EU, but not as a Sida activity. Though the labs have been well conducted, Sida assesses that due to the ongoing conflict this activity should not currently be prioritised. It will continue within the EU portfolio. International IDEA published a comparative study on the voting rights of IDPs in Sudan. The study was published on International IDEAs Website www.idea.int in both English and Arabic. The link to the published study was widely shared with the national partners, civil society, and other stakeholders concerned with the transitional process
